  dataApiUrl: process.env.NEON_DATA_API_URL!,

# Neon JS SDK - Import Reference

Complete import paths for all `@neondatabase` packages.

## @neondatabase/neon-js (Full SDK)

### Main Entry

```typescript
import {
  createClient,
  SupabaseAuthAdapter,
  BetterAuthVanillaAdapter
} from "@neondatabase/neon-js";
```

### Auth Subpaths

```typescript
// Next.js integration
import { authApiHandler, createAuthClient, neonAuth } from "@neondatabase/neon-js/auth/next";

// React adapters (NOT from main entry)
import { BetterAuthReactAdapter } from "@neondatabase/neon-js/auth/react/adapters";

// Vanilla adapters (also available from main entry)
import { BetterAuthVanillaAdapter, SupabaseAuthAdapter } from "@neondatabase/neon-js/auth/vanilla/adapters";
```

### UI Components

```typescript
// React UI components
import {
  NeonAuthUIProvider,
  AuthView,
  SignInForm,
  SignUpForm,
  UserButton,
  UserAvatar,
  ForgotPasswordForm,
  ResetPasswordForm,
  MagicLinkForm,
  TwoFactorForm,
  SettingsCard
} from "@neondatabase/neon-js/auth/react/ui";

// Server utilities (for Next.js page generation)
import { authViewPaths } from "@neondatabase/neon-js/auth/react/ui/server";
```

### UI CSS

```typescript
// Without Tailwind - pre-built CSS bundle (~47KB)
import "@neondatabase/neon-js/ui/css";
```

```css
/* With Tailwind v4 - token definitions only (~2KB) */
@import 'tailwindcss';
@import '@neondatabase/neon-js/ui/tailwind';
```

**Never import both** - causes duplicate styles.

## @neondatabase/auth (Auth Only)

Smaller bundle when you don't need database queries.

### Main Entry

```typescript
import { createAuthClient } from "@neondatabase/auth";
```

### Adapters

```typescript
// React adapter (NOT from main entry)
import { BetterAuthReactAdapter } from "@neondatabase/auth/react/adapters";

// Vanilla adapters
import { BetterAuthVanillaAdapter, SupabaseAuthAdapter } from "@neondatabase/auth/vanilla/adapters";
```

### Next.js Integration

```typescript
import { authApiHandler, createAuthClient, neonAuth } from "@neondatabase/auth/next";
```

### UI Components

```typescript
import { NeonAuthUIProvider, AuthView, SignInForm } from "@neondatabase/auth/react/ui";
import { authViewPaths } from "@neondatabase/auth/react/ui/server";
```

### UI CSS

```typescript
import "@neondatabase/auth/ui/css";
```

## @neondatabase/postgrest-js (Data Only)

Use when bringing your own authentication.

```typescript
import { NeonPostgrestClient, fetchWithToken } from "@neondatabase/postgrest-js";

const client = new NeonPostgrestClient({
  dataApiUrl: process.env.NEON_DATA_API_URL!,
  options: {
    global: {
      fetch: fetchWithToken(async () => getTokenFromYourAuthSystem()),
    },
  },
});
```

## Import Rules Summary

| Export | Main Entry | Subpath Required |
|--------|------------|------------------|
| `createClient` | Yes | No |
| `SupabaseAuthAdapter` | Yes | No |
| `BetterAuthVanillaAdapter` | Yes | No |
| `BetterAuthReactAdapter` | **No** | `auth/react/adapters` |
| `createAuthClient` (Next.js) | **No** | `auth/next` |
| `authApiHandler` | **No** | `auth/next` |
| `NeonAuthUIProvider` | **No** | `auth/react/ui` |
| UI CSS | **No** | `ui/css` or `ui/tailwind` |

## Common Import Mistakes

### Wrong: BetterAuthReactAdapter from main

```typescript
// This will NOT work
import { BetterAuthReactAdapter } from "@neondatabase/neon-js";
```

### Correct: BetterAuthReactAdapter from subpath

```typescript
// This works
import { BetterAuthReactAdapter } from "@neondatabase/neon-js/auth/react/adapters";
```

### Wrong: Both CSS imports

```css
/* Causes ~94KB of duplicate styles */
@import '@neondatabase/neon-js/ui/css';
@import '@neondatabase/neon-js/ui/tailwind';
```

### Correct: One CSS import

```css
/* Without Tailwind */
@import '@neondatabase/neon-js/ui/css';

/* OR with Tailwind v4 */
@import 'tailwindcss';
@import '@neondatabase/neon-js/ui/tailwind';
```

Neon JS SDK - UI Theming

Complete guide to customizing the Neon Auth UI components.

How It Works

Neon Auth UI automatically inherits your app's existing theme. If you already have CSS variables like --primary, --background, etc. defined (from Tailwind, shadcn/ui, or custom CSS), the auth components will use them with no configuration needed.

Key features:

  • Automatic inheritance: Uses your existing --primary, --background, etc. variables
  • Fallback defaults: If you don't define a variable, sensible defaults are used
  • No conflicts: All auth styles are in @layer neon-auth, so your styles always win
  • Import order doesn't matter: CSS layers handle priority automatically

Integration with shadcn/ui

If you use shadcn/ui or similar libraries that define --primary, --background, etc., Neon Auth will automatically inherit those colors. No additional configuration needed.

Why Variables Are on :root

Variables are defined on :root to ensure they're accessible to portal-rendered components (modals, dropdowns, toasts) that render outside the normal component tree.

CSS Import Decision

Your Setup Import Path Bundle Size
No Tailwind @neondatabase/neon-js/ui/css ~47KB
Tailwind v4 @neondatabase/neon-js/ui/tailwind ~2KB (tokens only)

Never import both - causes duplicate styles (~94KB).

Import order doesn't matter - auth UI styles are wrapped in @layer neon-auth, giving your unlayered styles automatic priority.

Without Tailwind

// In layout.tsx or _app.tsx
import "@neondatabase/neon-js/ui/css";

With Tailwind v4

/* globals.css */
@import 'tailwindcss';
@import '@neondatabase/neon-js/ui/tailwind';

/* Your theme variables (if any) - auth will inherit these automatically */

Customization Options

Option 1: Use Your Existing Theme (Recommended)

If you already have theme variables defined, auth components inherit them automatically:

/* Your existing theme - auth uses these automatically */
:root {
  --primary: oklch(0.55 0.25 250);        /* Auth buttons will be blue */
  --primary-foreground: oklch(0.98 0 0);
  --background: oklch(1 0 0);
  --foreground: oklch(0.145 0 0);
  /* ... */
}

No additional configuration needed!

Option 2: Auth-Specific Customization

To customize auth components differently from your main app, use the --neon-* prefix:

:root {
  /* Your app's primary color */
  --primary: oklch(0.55 0.25 250);  /* Blue */

  /* Override just for auth components */
  --neon-primary: oklch(0.55 0.18 145);  /* Green - only auth uses this */
}

Variable Inherits From Default (Light)
--neon-primary --primary oklch(0.205 0 0)
--neon-primary-foreground --primary-foreground oklch(0.985 0 0)
--neon-secondary --secondary oklch(0.97 0 0)

--neon-muted-foreground --muted-foreground oklch(0.556 0 0)
--neon-accent --accent oklch(0.97 0 0)
--neon-accent-foreground --accent-foreground oklch(0.205 0 0)

--neon-radius --radius 0.625rem

Token Pairing Rules

Always override pairs together to maintain contrast (min 4.5:1 ratio).

Background Token Foreground Token
--primary --primary-foreground
--secondary --secondary-foreground
--background --foreground
--muted --muted-foreground
--accent --accent-foreground
--destructive --destructive-foreground
--card --card-foreground

If you only define --primary without --primary-foreground, contrast issues may occur.

Dark Mode

Dark Mode Fallback Behavior

If you define a variable in :root but not in .dark:

  • Light mode: Uses your value
  • Dark mode: Uses auth's default dark value

Recommendation: If customizing, define both light and dark modes.

Option 1: next-themes (Recommended for Next.js)

npm install next-themes

// app/layout.tsx
import { ThemeProvider } from "next-themes";

export default function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en" suppressHydrationWarning>
      <body>
        <ThemeProvider attribute="class" defaultTheme="system" enableSystem>
          {children}
        </ThemeProvider>
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}

// components/theme-toggle.tsx
"use client";
import { useTheme } from "next-themes";

export function ThemeToggle() {
  const { theme, setTheme } = useTheme();
  return (
    <button onClick={() => setTheme(theme === "dark" ? "light" : "dark")}>
      Toggle theme
    </button>
  );
}

Option 2: Vanilla JavaScript

// Check system preference
const prefersDark = window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches;

// Apply dark mode
document.documentElement.classList.toggle("dark", prefersDark);

// Toggle manually
function toggleDarkMode() {
  document.documentElement.classList.toggle("dark");
}

Option 3: CSS Only (System Preference)

@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
  :root {
    --background: oklch(0.145 0 0);
    --foreground: oklch(0.985 0 0);
    /* ... other dark tokens */
  }
}

OKLCH Color Format

Neon Auth UI uses OKLCH for perceptually uniform colors.

Format: oklch(L C H) or oklch(L C H / alpha)

Parameter Range Description
L (Lightness) 0-1 0 = black, 1 = white
C (Chroma) 0-0.4 0 = gray, higher = more vivid
H (Hue) 0-360 Color wheel degrees
alpha 0-1 or 0%-100% Opacity

Examples:

--primary: oklch(0.55 0.25 250);        /* Vivid blue */
--primary: oklch(0.55 0.25 250 / 50%);  /* 50% opacity */
--muted: oklch(0.5 0 0);                /* Neutral gray (no chroma) */

Convert HEX/RGB to OKLCH: https://oklch.com

Component-Specific Styling

All UI components accept classNames props for targeted customization:

import { SignInForm } from "@neondatabase/neon-js/auth/react/ui";

<SignInForm
  className="mx-auto max-w-md"
  classNames={{
    card: "border-primary/20",
    button: "rounded-full",
    input: "bg-muted/50",
  }}
/>

Available classNames Interfaces

  • AuthViewClassNames - Main auth view container
  • AuthFormClassNames - Form wrapper and fields
  • UserAvatarClassNames - Avatar component
  • UserButtonClassNames - User dropdown button
  • SettingsCardClassNames - Settings panels

Common Theming Mistakes

1. Importing Both CSS Paths

/* Wrong - duplicate styles, ~94KB */
@import '@neondatabase/neon-js/ui/css';
@import '@neondatabase/neon-js/ui/tailwind';

/* Correct - pick one */
@import '@neondatabase/neon-js/ui/css';

2. Missing Foreground Pairs

/* Wrong - white text on light background */
:root {
  --primary: oklch(0.9 0.1 250);
}

/* Correct - ensure contrast */
:root {
  --primary: oklch(0.9 0.1 250);
  --primary-foreground: oklch(0.1 0 0);
}

3. Using HEX/RGB Instead of OKLCH

/* Works but may not match perfectly */
:root {
  --primary: #3b82f6;
}

/* Recommended - use OKLCH format */
:root {
  --primary: oklch(0.59 0.2 262);
}

4. Forgetting Dark Mode Tokens

/* Wrong - light mode only */
:root {
  --primary: oklch(0.55 0.25 250);
  --primary-foreground: oklch(0.98 0 0);
}

/* Correct - both modes */
:root {
  --primary: oklch(0.55 0.25 250);
  --primary-foreground: oklch(0.98 0 0);
}
.dark {
  --primary: oklch(0.75 0.2 250);
  --primary-foreground: oklch(0.1 0 0);
}

# Neon JS SDK - UI Theming

Complete guide to customizing the Neon Auth UI components.

## How It Works

Neon Auth UI **automatically inherits your app's existing theme**. If you already have CSS variables like `--primary`, `--background`, etc. defined (from Tailwind, shadcn/ui, or custom CSS), the auth components will use them with no configuration needed.

**Key features:**
- **Automatic inheritance**: Uses your existing `--primary`, `--background`, etc. variables
- **Fallback defaults**: If you don't define a variable, sensible defaults are used
- **No conflicts**: All auth styles are in `@layer neon-auth`, so your styles always win
- **Import order doesn't matter**: CSS layers handle priority automatically

### Integration with shadcn/ui

If you use shadcn/ui or similar libraries that define `--primary`, `--background`, etc., Neon Auth will automatically inherit those colors. No additional configuration needed.

### Why Variables Are on `:root`

Variables are defined on `:root` to ensure they're accessible to portal-rendered components (modals, dropdowns, toasts) that render outside the normal component tree.

## CSS Import Decision

| Your Setup | Import Path | Bundle Size |
|------------|-------------|-------------|
| No Tailwind | `@neondatabase/neon-js/ui/css` | ~47KB |
| Tailwind v4 | `@neondatabase/neon-js/ui/tailwind` | ~2KB (tokens only) |

**Never import both** - causes duplicate styles (~94KB).

Import order doesn't matter - auth UI styles are wrapped in `@layer neon-auth`, giving your unlayered styles automatic priority.

### Without Tailwind

```typescript
// In layout.tsx or _app.tsx
import "@neondatabase/neon-js/ui/css";
```

### With Tailwind v4

```css
/* globals.css */
@import 'tailwindcss';
@import '@neondatabase/neon-js/ui/tailwind';

/* Your theme variables (if any) - auth will inherit these automatically */
```

## Customization Options

### Option 1: Use Your Existing Theme (Recommended)

If you already have theme variables defined, auth components inherit them automatically:

```css
/* Your existing theme - auth uses these automatically */
:root {
  --primary: oklch(0.55 0.25 250);        /* Auth buttons will be blue */
  --primary-foreground: oklch(0.98 0 0);
  --background: oklch(1 0 0);
  --foreground: oklch(0.145 0 0);
  /* ... */
}
```

No additional configuration needed!

### Option 2: Auth-Specific Customization

To customize auth components differently from your main app, use the `--neon-*` prefix:

```css
:root {
  /* Your app's primary color */
  --primary: oklch(0.55 0.25 250);  /* Blue */

  /* Override just for auth components */
  --neon-primary: oklch(0.55 0.18 145);  /* Green - only auth uses this */
}
```

### Complete `--neon-*` Variable Reference

| Variable | Inherits From | Default (Light) |
|----------|---------------|-----------------|
| `--neon-primary` | `--primary` | `oklch(0.205 0 0)` |
| `--neon-primary-foreground` | `--primary-foreground` | `oklch(0.985 0 0)` |
| `--neon-secondary` | `--secondary` | `oklch(0.97 0 0)` |
| `--neon-secondary-foreground` | `--secondary-foreground` | `oklch(0.205 0 0)` |
| `--neon-background` | `--background` | `oklch(1 0 0)` |
| `--neon-foreground` | `--foreground` | `oklch(0.145 0 0)` |
| `--neon-muted` | `--muted` | `oklch(0.97 0 0)` |
| `--neon-muted-foreground` | `--muted-foreground` | `oklch(0.556 0 0)` |
| `--neon-accent` | `--accent` | `oklch(0.97 0 0)` |
| `--neon-accent-foreground` | `--accent-foreground` | `oklch(0.205 0 0)` |
| `--neon-destructive` | `--destructive` | `oklch(0.577 0.245 27.325)` |
| `--neon-card` | `--card` | `oklch(1 0 0)` |
| `--neon-card-foreground` | `--card-foreground` | `oklch(0.145 0 0)` |
| `--neon-border` | `--border` | `oklch(0.922 0 0)` |
| `--neon-input` | `--input` | `oklch(0.922 0 0)` |
| `--neon-ring` | `--ring` | `oklch(0.708 0 0)` |
| `--neon-radius` | `--radius` | `0.625rem` |

## Token Pairing Rules

**Always override pairs together** to maintain contrast (min 4.5:1 ratio).

| Background Token | Foreground Token |
|-----------------|------------------|
| `--primary` | `--primary-foreground` |
| `--secondary` | `--secondary-foreground` |
| `--background` | `--foreground` |
| `--muted` | `--muted-foreground` |
| `--accent` | `--accent-foreground` |
| `--destructive` | `--destructive-foreground` |
| `--card` | `--card-foreground` |

If you only define `--primary` without `--primary-foreground`, contrast issues may occur.

## Dark Mode

### Dark Mode Fallback Behavior

If you define a variable in `:root` but not in `.dark`:
- **Light mode**: Uses your value
- **Dark mode**: Uses auth's default dark value

**Recommendation**: If customizing, define both light and dark modes.

### Option 1: next-themes (Recommended for Next.js)

```bash
npm install next-themes
```

```typescript
// app/layout.tsx
import { ThemeProvider } from "next-themes";

export default function Layout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="en" suppressHydrationWarning>
      <body>
        <ThemeProvider attribute="class" defaultTheme="system" enableSystem>
          {children}
        </ThemeProvider>
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

```typescript
// components/theme-toggle.tsx
"use client";
import { useTheme } from "next-themes";

export function ThemeToggle() {
  const { theme, setTheme } = useTheme();
  return (
    <button onClick={() => setTheme(theme === "dark" ? "light" : "dark")}>
      Toggle theme
    </button>
  );
}
```

### Option 2: Vanilla JavaScript

```typescript
// Check system preference
const prefersDark = window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches;

// Apply dark mode
document.documentElement.classList.toggle("dark", prefersDark);

// Toggle manually
function toggleDarkMode() {
  document.documentElement.classList.toggle("dark");
}
```

### Option 3: CSS Only (System Preference)

```css
@media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) {
  :root {
    --background: oklch(0.145 0 0);
    --foreground: oklch(0.985 0 0);
    /* ... other dark tokens */
  }
}
```

## OKLCH Color Format

Neon Auth UI uses OKLCH for perceptually uniform colors.

**Format:** `oklch(L C H)` or `oklch(L C H / alpha)`

| Parameter | Range | Description |
|-----------|-------|-------------|
| L (Lightness) | 0-1 | 0 = black, 1 = white |
| C (Chroma) | 0-0.4 | 0 = gray, higher = more vivid |
| H (Hue) | 0-360 | Color wheel degrees |
| alpha | 0-1 or 0%-100% | Opacity |

**Examples:**

```css
--primary: oklch(0.55 0.25 250);        /* Vivid blue */
--primary: oklch(0.55 0.25 250 / 50%);  /* 50% opacity */
--muted: oklch(0.5 0 0);                /* Neutral gray (no chroma) */
```

**Convert HEX/RGB to OKLCH:** https://oklch.com

## Component-Specific Styling

All UI components accept `classNames` props for targeted customization:

```typescript
import { SignInForm } from "@neondatabase/neon-js/auth/react/ui";

<SignInForm
  className="mx-auto max-w-md"
  classNames={{
    card: "border-primary/20",
    button: "rounded-full",
    input: "bg-muted/50",
  }}
/>
```

### Available classNames Interfaces

- `AuthViewClassNames` - Main auth view container
- `AuthFormClassNames` - Form wrapper and fields
- `UserAvatarClassNames` - Avatar component
- `UserButtonClassNames` - User dropdown button
- `SettingsCardClassNames` - Settings panels

## Common Theming Mistakes

### 1. Importing Both CSS Paths

```css
/* Wrong - duplicate styles, ~94KB */
@import '@neondatabase/neon-js/ui/css';
@import '@neondatabase/neon-js/ui/tailwind';

/* Correct - pick one */
@import '@neondatabase/neon-js/ui/css';
```

### 2. Missing Foreground Pairs

```css
/* Wrong - white text on light background */
:root {
  --primary: oklch(0.9 0.1 250);
}

/* Correct - ensure contrast */
:root {
  --primary: oklch(0.9 0.1 250);
  --primary-foreground: oklch(0.1 0 0);
}
```

### 3. Using HEX/RGB Instead of OKLCH

```css
/* Works but may not match perfectly */
:root {
  --primary: #3b82f6;
}

/* Recommended - use OKLCH format */
:root {
  --primary: oklch(0.59 0.2 262);
}
```

### 4. Forgetting Dark Mode Tokens

```css
/* Wrong - light mode only */
:root {
  --primary: oklch(0.55 0.25 250);
  --primary-foreground: oklch(0.98 0 0);
}

/* Correct - both modes */
:root {
  --primary: oklch(0.55 0.25 250);
  --primary-foreground: oklch(0.98 0 0);
}
.dark {
  --primary: oklch(0.75 0.2 250);
  --primary-foreground: oklch(0.1 0 0);
}
```

## Brand Color Examples

```css
:root {
  --primary: oklch(0.59 0.2 262);
  --primary-foreground: oklch(0.98 0 0);
}
.dark {
  --primary: oklch(0.7 0.18 262);
  --primary-foreground: oklch(0.1 0 0);
}
```

### Green Theme

  --primary: oklch(0.55 0.18 145);
  --primary-foreground: oklch(0.98 0 0);
}
.dark {
  --primary: oklch(0.7 0.16 145);
  --primary-foreground: oklch(0.1 0 0);
}
```

### Purple Theme

```css

  --primary: oklch(0.55 0.22 300);
  --primary-foreground: oklch(0.98 0 0);
}
.dark {
  --primary: oklch(0.7 0.2 300);
  --primary-foreground: oklch(0.1 0 0);

Content has moved to [neondatabase/agent-skills](https://github.com/neondatabase/agent-skills).\n\n## Project Overview\n\nThis repository contains a comprehensive suite of AI-powered development tools for Neon, including:\n\n1. **Context Rules** (`.mdc` files): Markdown Context files that guide AI systems\n2. **Claude Code Plugin**: Full-featured plugin with guided skills and MCP server integration\n3. **Neon SDK Rules**: Guidelines for TypeScript and Python SDKs\n\nThe primary audience includes AI developers using Claude, Cursor, and other AI-powered code assistants who work with Neon databases.\n\n## Repository Structure\n\n```\n.\n├── *.mdc                          # Context rule files (16 total)\n├── .claude-plugin/\n│   └── marketplace.json           # Marketplace metadata\n├── neon-plugin/                   # Claude Code plugin\n│   ├── .claude-plugin/\n│   │   └── plugin.json            # Plugin metadata\n│   ├── .mcp.json                  # MCP server Documentation reference installer\n│       ├── neon-auth/             # Neon Auth integration\n│       │   ├── guides/            # Setup guides (Next.js, React SPA)\n│       │   └── templates/         # Auth client templates\n│       ├── neon-drizzle/\n│       │   ├── guides/            # Step-by-step workflow guides\n│       │   ├── references/        # Technical reference docs\n│       │   ├── scripts/           # Utility scripts\n│       │   └── templates/         # Code templates\n│       ├── neon-js/               # Full Neon JS SDK integration\n│       │   ├── guides/            # Setup guides\n│       │   └── templates/         # Client templates\n│       ├── neon-serverless/\n│       └── neon-toolkit/\n├── references/                    # Shared technical reference docs (16 files)\n│   ├── code-generation-rules.md\n│   ├── neon-auth-*.md             # Auth-related references (11 files)\n│   │   # Includes: common-mistakes, components, provider-config,\n│   │   # setup (general, nextjs, nodejs, react-spa), troubleshooting,\n│   │   # ui (general, nextjs, react-spa)\n│   └── neon-js-*.md               # Neon JS references (4 files)\n│       # Includes: adapters, data-api, imports, theming\n├── mcp-prompts/                   # MCP prompt templates\n├── .claude/\n│   └── settings.local.json        # Local Claude Code settings\n├── .serena/                       # Serena code intelligence cache\n├── CHANGELOG.md                   # Version history and release notes\n├── CONTRIBUTING.md                # Contribution guidelines\n├── LICENSE                        # MIT License\n├── README.md                      # User-facing documentation\n└── CLAUDE.md                      # This file\n\n```\n\n## Context Rules (.mdc files)\n\n### Getting Started (2 files)\n- **neon-get-started.mdc**: Interactive onboarding guide for Neon projects\n- **neon-get-started-kiro.mdc**: Kiro-specific onboarding guide\n\n### Core Integration Rules (5 files)\n- **neon-auth.mdc**: Neon Auth integration with `@neondatabase/auth` package\n- **neon-js.mdc**: Full Neon JS SDK with `@neondatabase/neon-js` package\n- **neon-serverless.mdc**: Serverless database connections and pooling\n- **neon-drizzle.mdc**: Drizzle ORM integration with Neon\n- **neon-toolkit.mdc**: Ephemeral database creation for testing\n\n### SDK Rules (2 files)\n- **neon-typescript-sdk.mdc**: TypeScript SDK usage patterns\n- **neon-python-sdk.mdc**: Python SDK usage patterns\n\n### API Rules (7 files)\n- **neon-api-guidelines.mdc**: General API best practices\n- **neon-api-projects.mdc**: Project management API\n- **neon-api-branches.mdc**: Branch management API\n- **neon-api-endpoints.mdc**: Compute endpoint management API\n- **neon-api-organizations.mdc**: Organization and role management API\n- **neon-api-keys.mdc**: API key and authentication management\n- **neon-api-operations.mdc**: Operation execution and monitoring\n\n## Claude Code Plugin Structure\n\n### Plugin Configuration\n- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`: Contains plugin metadata (name, version, description)\n- `.mcp.json`: Configures connection to Neon's remote MCP server\n\n### Skills Directory\nEach skill is self-contained with multiple components:\n\n1. **SKILL.md**: Describes the skill's purpose and workflow\n2. **scripts/**: Executable utilities for the skill (TypeScript or shell)\n3. **templates/**: Code examples and templates\n4. **guides/** (optional): Step-by-step guides for different scenarios\n5. **references/** (optional): Technical reference documentation\n\n#### Neon Drizzle Skill\n- **Purpose**: Drizzle ORM setup and database management with comprehensive workflow support\n- **Scripts**: `generate-schema.ts`, `run-migration.ts`\n- **Templates**: Schema examples, drizzle config (HTTP and WebSocket adapters)\n- **Guides**:\n  - `new-project.md`: Setting up Drizzle in new projects\n  - `existing-project.md`: Integrating Drizzle into existing codebases\n  - `schema-only.md`: Schema-first workflow without migrations\n  - `troubleshooting.md`: Common issues and solutions\n- **References**:\n  - `adapters.md`: HTTP vs WebSocket adapter selection\n  - `migrations.md`: Migration strategies and patterns\n  - `query-patterns.md`: Common query patterns and best practices\n\n#### Neon Serverless Skill\n- **Purpose**: Serverless database connection configuration\n- **Scripts**: `validate-connection.ts`\n- **Templates**: HTTP connection, WebSocket pool\n\n#### Neon Auth Skill\n- **Purpose**: Neon Auth integration using `@neondatabase/auth` package\n- **Guides**:\n  - `nextjs-setup.md`: Next.js App Router setup with auth integration\n  - `react-spa-setup.md`: React SPA setup with auth integration\n- **Templates**: Auth client configuration, Next.js API route handler\n\n#### Neon JS Skill\n- **Purpose**: Full Neon JS SDK integration using `@neondatabase/neon-js` package\n- **Guides**:\n  - `setup.md`: Complete setup guide for neon-js\n- **Templates**: Full client configuration with auth + data API\n\n#### Neon Toolkit Skill\n- **Purpose**: Ephemeral database creation for testing and CI/CD workflows\n- **Scripts**: `create-ephemeral-db.ts`, `destroy-ephemeral-db.ts`\n- **Templates**: Toolkit workflow\n\n#### Add Neon Docs Skill\n- **Purpose**: Install Neon documentation references in project AI configuration files\n- **Workflow**: `install-knowledge.md` with step-by-step reference installation process\n- **Metadata**: `skill-knowledge-map.json` defining available documentation references\n- **Target Files**: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, or Cursor rules files\n\n## Key Patterns & Conventions\n\n### .mdc File Format\n- Each .mdc file uses Markdown with practical code examples\n- Files follow a consistent structure: Overview → Use Cases → Examples → Best Practices\n- Files are tool-agnostic and can be used in multiple AI environments\n\n### Skill Organization\n- Skills are self-contained workflows with guided steps\n- Templates are production-ready examples\n- Scripts provide automation and validation\n\n### Plugin Metadata\n- Version follows semantic versioning\n- Plugin description clearly indicates purpose and scope\n- MCP configuration uses remote URL for centralized updates\n\n## Usage Context\n\n### For Claude Code Users\n- Activate the plugin in Claude Code\n- Use skills for guided workflows\n- MCP server provides real-time Neon resource management\n\n### For Other AI Tools\n- Copy .mdc files to tool-specific rule directories\n- Files work with Cursor, custom ChatGPT instances, etc.\n- Each file is self-contained and doesn't require dependencies\n\n### For Contributors\n- Add new .mdc files for new technologies or patterns\n- Update skills with new templates or scripts\n- Keep plugin.json version in sync with major updates\n\n## Recent Changes & Decisions\n\n### Repository Archived (January 2026)\n- Repository archived; content moved to [neondatabase/agent-skills](https://github.com/neondatabase/agent-skills)\n- New repository follows Agent Skills specification supported by major agents and editors\n- Install via: `npx skills add neondatabase/agent-skills`\n\n### Version 1.1.0 Release (December 9, 2025)\n- Added **neon-auth** skill for Neon Auth integration with `@neondatabase/auth`\n  - Next.js setup guide with full workflow\n  - React SPA setup guide\n  - Templates: API route handler, auth client\n- Added **neon-js** skill for full Neon JS SDK with `@neondatabase/neon-js`\n  - Setup guide with auth + data API integration\n  - Template: unified client configuration\n- Added shared `references/` directory with technical documentation:\n  - `neon-auth-*.md` files: Auth components, provider config, troubleshooting, common mistakes, UI\n  - `neon-js-*.md` files: Adapters, data API, imports, theming\n  - `code-generation-rules.md`: Code generation best practices\n- Added `mcp-prompts/` directory for MCP prompt templates\n- Added neon-auth.mdc and neon-js.mdc context rules\n- Added neon-get-started.mdc and neon-get-started-kiro.mdc for onboarding\n- Total .mdc files increased from 13 to 16\n- Total skills increased from 4 to 6\n- Updated skill-knowledge-map.json with new skills\n\n### Version 1.0.1 Release (October 29, 2025)\n- Added evals to the `neon-drizzle` and `add-neon-docs` skills\n- Fixed `add-neon-docs` skill description for proper activation\n- Added explicit rules to prevent unwanted file edits\n\n### Version 1.0.0 Release (October 23, 2025)\n- First public release of the Neon Claude Code Plugin\n- Added CHANGELOG.md for version tracking\n- Added CONTRIBUTING.md with contribution guidelines\n- Restructured marketplace to follow Claude Code best practices\n  - Marketplace at repository root (`.claude-plugin/marketplace.json`)\n  - Plugin directory at repository root (`neon-plugin/`)\n- Implemented 4 guided skills:\n  - **neon-drizzle**: Drizzle ORM with comprehensive workflow guides (new projects, existing projects, schema-only)\n  - **neon-serverless**: Serverless connection configuration\n  - **neon-toolkit**: Ephemeral database management\n  - **add-neon-docs**: Documentation reference installer\n- Enhanced Drizzle skill with:\n  - Step-by-step workflow guides for different scenarios\n  - Technical references (adapters, migrations, query patterns)\n  - Migration scripts and standard `db:*` npm scripts\n- Configured MCP server integration for resource management (https://mcp.neon.tech/mcp)\n- Published 13 context rules (.mdc files) covering core integrations, SDKs, and API patterns\n\n### API Rules Addition (Previous)\n- Added 7 comprehensive API rule files\n- Organized API rules by resource type (projects, branches, endpoints, etc.)\n- Provides patterns for REST API usage\n\n### SDK Rules Addition\n- Added TypeScript and Python SDK rule files\n- Guides for programmatic database management\n\n## Important Notes for Future Work\n\n1. **Keep .mdc files separate**: Each .mdc file should remain independent and not reference others\n2. **Plugin versioning**: Update plugin.json version when adding new skills\n3. **MCP server**: The remote MCP server URL should be kept current (https://mcp.neon.tech/mcp)\n4. **Template testing**: Test new skill templates in real Claude Code environments before committing\n5. **Documentation sync**: Update README.md and CLAUDE.md when adding new rules or skills\n\n## Technology Stack\n\n- **Language**: Markdown (for .mdc files), TypeScript (for scripts and templates)\n- **Runtimes**: Node.js (for scripts), Shell (for setup)\n- **Tools**: Claude Code, Cursor, custom AI environments\n- **Integration**: MCP (Model Context Protocol) for resource management\n\n## https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/best-practices\n- **Plugin Marketplace**: https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/plugin-marketplaces\n\nThese resources provide       "rawContent": "# Changelog\n\nAll notable changes to the Neon Claude Code Plugin will be documented in this file.\n\nThe format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),\nand this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).\n\n## [1.1.0] - 2025-12-09\n\n### Added\n- **neon-auth** skill for Neon Auth integration with `@neondatabase/auth`\n  - Next.js App Router setup guide\n  - React SPA setup guide\n  - Templates: API route handler, auth client\n- **neon-js** skill for full Neon JS SDK with `@neondatabase/neon-js`\n  - Setup guide with auth + data API integration\n  - Template: unified client configuration\n- New context rules:\n  - `neon-auth.mdc` - Neon Auth integration patterns\n  - `neon-js.mdc` - Neon JS SDK patterns\n  - `neon-get-started.mdc` - Interactive onboarding guide\n  - `neon-get-started-kiro.mdc` - Kiro-specific onboarding\n- Shared `references/` directory with technical documentation\n- `mcp-prompts/` directory for MCP prompt templates\n- Added neon-auth and neon-js entries to skill-knowledge-map.json\n\n### Changed\n- Updated cross-references in existing skills to include neon-auth\n- Removed users_sync table references from auth documentation (deprecated feature)\n- Consolidated duplicate content into single source of truth\n\n## [1.0.1] - 2025-10-29\n\n- Added evals to the `neon-drizzle` and `add-neon-docs` skills\n- Fixed `add-neon-docs` skill description, so it is picked properly\n- Added explicit rules so that `add-neon-docs` skill doesn't edit unwanted files\n\n\n## [1.0.0] - 2025-10-23\n\n### Added\n- Initial public release\n- **neon-drizzle** skill with comprehensive guides (new projects, existing projects, schema-only)\n- **neon-serverless** skill for connection configuration\n- **neon-toolkit** skill for ephemeral database management\n- **add-neon-docs** skill for documentation reference installation\n- MCP server integration for resource management\n- 13 context rules (.mdc files) covering:\n  - Core integrations (auth, serverless, drizzle, toolkit)\n  - SDKs (TypeScript, Python)\n  - API guidelines (projects, branches, endpoints, organizations, keys, operations)\n- Templates and scripts for all skills\n- Comprehensive technical references for Drizzle (adapters, migrations, query patterns)\n\n### Documentation\n- Complete README with installation instructions\n- Individual SKILL.md files for each skill\n- Step-by-step workflow guides\n- Technical reference documentation\n\n[1.0.0]: https://github.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules/releases/tag/v1.0.0\n",

      "contentPreview": "Thank you for your interest in contributing to the Neon Claude Code Plugin!\nUse GitHub Issues for bug reports and feature requests\nProvide clear reproduction steps for bugs\nInclude relevant environment information (Claude Code version, OS)\nTo add a new skill:\n1. **Create skill directory**: \n2. **Add",
      "rawContent": "# Contributing to Neon Claude Code Plugin\n\nThank you for your interest in contributing to the Neon Claude Code Plugin!\n\n## How to Contribute\n\n### Reporting Issues\n\n- Use GitHub Issues for bug reports and feature requests\n- Provide clear reproduction steps for bugs\n- Include relevant environment information (Claude Code version, OS)\n\n### Contributing Skills\n\nTo add a new skill:\n\n1. **Create skill directory**: `neon-plugin/skills/your-skill-name/`\n2. **Add SKILL.md**: Follow the front matter format (see existing skills)\n3. **Include components**:\n   - `templates/` - Code examples and templates\n   - `scripts/` - Utility scripts\n   - `guides/` (optional) - Step-by-step workflows\n   - `references/` (optional) - Technical documentation\n4. **Test thoroughly**: Verify skill loads and executes correctly in Claude Code\n5. **Update documentation**: Add skill to main README\n\n### Contributing Context Rules\n\nTo add or update `.mdc` files:\n\n1. **Follow existing format**: Overview → Use Cases → Examples → Best Practices\n2. **Keep files focused**: One technology/pattern per file\n3. **Include practical examples**: Real-world code snippets\n4. **Test with AI tools**: Verify rules work with Claude Code and Cursor\n5. **Tool-agnostic**: Don't reference specific AI tools in the content\n\n### Pull Request Process\n\n1. Fork the repository\n2. Create a feature branch: `git checkout -b feature/your-feature-name`\n3. Make your changes\n4. Test locally (see Testing section)\n5. Commit with clear messages: `git commit -m \"Add: new skill for XYZ\"`\n6. Push to your fork: `git push origin feature/your-feature-name`\n7. Open a Pull Request with:\n   - Clear description of changes\n   - Link to related issues\n   - Testing steps performed\n\n### Testing\n\nBefore submitting a PR:\n\n1. **JSON validation**:\n   ```bash\n   jq . .claude-plugin/marketplace.json\n   jq . neon-plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json\n   ```\n\n2. **Local testing**:\n   - Test marketplace installation locally\n   - Verify all skills load correctly\n   - Test MCP server connection\n   - Run through skill workflows\n\n3. **Documentation**:\n   - Check markdown rendering\n   - Verify all links work\n   - Ensure code examples are correct\n\n### Code Style\n\n- **Markdown**: Use consistent formatting (fenced code blocks, proper headings)\n- **JSON**: 2-space indentation, sorted keys where logical\n- **TypeScript/JavaScript**: Follow existing code style in templates and scripts\n- **File naming**: kebab-case for files and directories\n\n## Development Setup\n\n1. Clone the repository:\n   ```bash\n   git clone https://github.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules.git\n   cd ai-rules\n   ```\n\n2. Test locally in Claude Code:\n   ```\n   /plugin marketplace add /absolute/path/to/ai-rules\n   /plugin install neon-plugin@neon\n   ```\n\n3. Make changes and reload:\n   ```\n   /plugin reload neon-plugin\n   ```\n\n## Running Evals\n\nEvals (evaluations) help test skills automatically using the `code-agent-eval` package. Each skill has its own eval directory in `neon-plugin/evals/`.\n\n### Prerequisites\n\nInstall dependencies:\n```bash\nbun install\n```\n\n### Running an Eval\n\nTo run a specific eval:\n```bash\nbun run neon-plugin/evals/{skill-name}/{skill-name}.eval.ts\n```\n\n**Examples:**\n```bash\n# Run Neon Drizzle skill eval\nbun run neon-plugin/evals/neon-drizzle-skill/neon-drizzle-skill.eval.ts\n\n# Run Add Neon Knowledge skill eval\nbun run neon-plugin/evals/add-neon-knowledge-skill/add-neon-knowledge-skill.eval.ts\n```\n\n### Eval Structure\n\nEach eval directory contains:\n- `{skill-name}.eval.ts` - The eval script\n- `eval-input/` - Test project input\n- `eval-results/` - Eval results (generated)\n\n### Creating New Evals\n\nWhen adding a new skill:\n\n1. **Create eval directory**: `neon-plugin/evals/{skill-name}/`\n2. **Add eval script**: `{skill-name}.eval.ts`\n3. **Create test input**: `eval-input/` with minimal project setup\n4. **Configure scorers**: Use built-in scorers or create custom ones\n5. **Test locally**: Run the eval to verify it works\n\nSee existing eval files for examples of configuration and scoring.\n\n## Questions?\n\n- Open a GitHub Issue for technical questions\n- Join our Discord for community discussion (link in README)\n\n## License\n\nBy contributing, you agree that your contributions will be licensed under the MIT License.\n",

      "contentPreview": "> Interactive guide for setting up Neon JS SDK (auth + database queries). Supports Next.js, Vite/React, and Node.js.\n**Be concise**: Report actions with checkmarks: \"✓ Installed @neondatabase/neon-js\"\n**Ask clearly**: \"Which framework are you using?\" instead of long explanations\n**Follow sequentiall",
      "rawContent": "# Neon JS SDK Setup (MCP Prompt Template)\n\n> Interactive guide for setting up Neon JS SDK (auth + database queries). Supports Next.js, Vite/React, and Node.js.\n\n## Communication Style\n\n- **Be concise**: Report actions with checkmarks: \"✓ Installed @neondatabase/neon-js\"\n- **Ask clearly**: \"Which framework are you using?\" instead of long explanations\n- **Follow sequentially**: Complete one step before moving to the next\n- **Allow pausing**: User can pause and resume anytime\n- **Progressive disclosure**: Load detailed guides only when needed\n\n---\n\n## Step 1: Provision Neon Auth\n\nBefore starting, provision Neon Auth for the user's project.\n\n**Check for provided context:**\n- Project ID: (check if provided via MCP args)\n- Branch ID: (optional, defaults to main branch)\n- Database Name: (optional, defaults to neondb)\n\n**If no project ID provided:**\n\n1. Check the user's projects using `list_projects` tool\n\n2. **If they have NO projects:**\n   - Ask if they want to create one\n   - Guide them to console.neon.tech or use `create_project` tool\n\n3. **If they have 1 project:**\n   - Ask: \"Want to add Neon Auth to '{project_name}'?\"\n\n4. **If they have multiple projects:**\n   - List project names and ask which one to use\n\n**Once project is confirmed, provision Neon Auth:**\n\nUse the `provision_neon_auth` tool with:\n- `projectId`: The selected project ID\n- `branchId`: (optional) defaults to main branch\n- `databaseName`: (optional) defaults to neondb\n\n**Save the `base_url` and `data_api_url` from the response** - you'll need them for Step 5.\n\n---\n\n## Step 2: Detect Project Context\n\nAutomatically detect the user's environment:\n\n**Framework Detection:**\n```bash\n# Check for Next.js App Router\nls app/layout.tsx app/page.tsx\n\n# Check for Vite/React\nls vite.config.ts src/main.tsx\n\n# Check for Node.js backend\nls package.json | grep -E '(express|fastify|koa)'\n```\n\n**Existing Setup:**\n```bash\n# Check if already installed\ngrep '@neondatabase' package.json\n\n# Check for existing setup\nls app/api/auth lib/db lib/auth 2>/dev/null\n```\n\n**Package Manager:**\n```bash\n# Detect from lock files\nls package-lock.json bun.lockb pnpm-lock.yaml yarn.lock\n```\n\n**Tailwind Detection:**\n```bash\n# Check for Tailwind config\nls tailwind.config.js tailwind.config.ts 2>/dev/null\n```\n\n---\n\n## Step 3: Package Confirmation\n\nThis setup installs `@neondatabase/neon-js` which includes:\n- ✅ Authentication (BetterAuth API)\n- ✅ Data API (PostgREST-style queries)\n- ✅ UI components (optional)\n\n**If user only needs auth** (no database queries):\n- Recommend switching to `@neondatabase/auth` (smaller bundle)\n- Load auth-only reference:\n  - https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules/main/references/neon-auth-setup.md\n\n**Otherwise, continue with this guide.**\n\n---\n\n## Step 4: Install Dependencies\n\n**Check package.json first**, then install:\n\n```bash\nnpm install @neondatabase/neon-js\n```\n\nReplace `npm install` with your detected package manager (`pnpm add`, `yarn add`, `bun add`).\n\n---\n\n## Step 5: Configure Environment Variables\n\n**Load setup reference for environment variables:**\nhttps://raw.githubusercontent.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules/main/references/neon-auth-setup.md#environment-variables\n\n**Quick reference:**\n\n**For Next.js** - Create/update `.env.local`:\n```bash\nNEON_AUTH_BASE_URL=<base_url_from_step_1>\nNEXT_PUBLIC_NEON_AUTH_URL=<base_url_from_step_1>\nNEON_DATA_API_URL=<data_api_url_from_step_1>\n```\n\n**For Vite** - Create/update `.env`:\n```bash\nVITE_NEON_AUTH_URL=<base_url_from_step_1>\nVITE_NEON_DATA_API_URL=<data_api_url_from_step_1>\n```\n\n**For Create React App** - Create/update `.env`:\n```bash\nREACT_APP_NEON_AUTH_URL=<base_url_from_step_1>\nREACT_APP_NEON_DATA_API_URL=<data_api_url_from_step_1>\n```\n\n**Important:** Add `.env*` to `.gitignore` if not already present.\n\n---\n\n## Step 6: Create Client\n\n**Load the comprehensive setup guide:**\n\n### Next.js App Router\n\n**Load guide:**\nhttps://raw.githubusercontent.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules/main/neon-plugin/skills/neon-js/guides/setup.md\n\n**Or load framework-specific sections:**\n- Auth setup: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules/main/references/neon-auth-setup.md#nextjs-app-router\n- Database client: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules/main/references/neon-js-data-api.md#client-setup\n\n### React SPA (Vite, Create React App)\n\n**Load guide:**\nhttps://raw.githubusercontent.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules/main/neon-plugin/skills/neon-js/guides/setup.md\n\n**Or load framework-specific sections:**\n- Auth setup: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules/main/references/neon-auth-setup.md#react-spa\n- Database client: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules/main/references/neon-js-data-api.md#client-setup\n\n### Node.js Backend\n\n**Load framework-specific sections:**\n- Auth setup: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules/main/references/neon-auth-setup.md#nodejs-backend\n- Database client: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules/main/references/neon-js-data-api.md#client-setup\n\n---\n\n## Step 7: Add Auth UI (Optional)\n\nAsk: \"Want to add pre-built auth UI components? (sign-in, sign-up forms, user button, account settings)\"\n\n**If yes**, load the UI setup guide:\nhttps://raw.githubusercontent.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules/main/references/neon-auth-ui.md\n\n**Key points:**\n- Import CSS (choose ONE method based on Tailwind detection)\n- Create Auth Provider with navigation adapters\n- Add routes for auth pages\n\n---\n\n## Step 8: Database Query Patterns\n\nOnce client is configured, guide user through PostgREST query syntax:\n\n**Load query reference:**\nhttps://raw.githubusercontent.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules/main/references/neon-js-data-api.md#query-patterns\n\n**Quick examples:**\n\n```typescript\n// Select with filters\nconst { data } = await client.from(\"items\")\n  .select(\"id, name, status\")\n  .eq(\"status\", \"active\")\n  .order(\"created_at\", { ascending: false })\n  .limit(10);\n\n// Insert\nconst { data, error } = await client.from(\"items\")\n  .insert({ name: \"New Item\", status: \"pending\" })\n  .select()\n  .single();\n```\n\n---\n\n## Step 9: Type Generation (Optional)\n\nOffer to generate TypeScript types from database schema:\n\n**Load type generation guide:**\nhttps://raw.githubusercontent.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules/main/references/neon-js-data-api.md#type-generation\n\n**Quick command:**\n```bash\nnpx neon-js gen-types --db-url \"postgresql://user:pass@host/db\" --output lib/db/database.types.ts\n```\n\n---\n\n## Step 10: Validation & Testing\n\n**Load validation checklist:**\nhttps://raw.githubusercontent.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules/main/neon-plugin/skills/neon-js/guides/setup.md#phase-8-validation--testing\n\n**Manual Testing Checklist:**\n- [ ] Auth: Sign up a test user\n- [ ] Auth: Sign in with test user\n- [ ] Auth: Verify session persists\n- [ ] Data: Query returns results\n- [ ] Data: Insert creates records\n- [ ] Data: Update modifies records\n\n**Having Issues?** See:\n- [Troubleshooting Guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules/main/references/neon-auth-troubleshooting.md)\n- [Common Mistakes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules/main/references/neon-auth-common-mistakes.md)\n- [Data API Error Handling](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules/main/references/neon-js-data-api.md#error-handling)\n\n---\n\n## Step 11: What's Next\n\nOnce setup is complete:\n\n\"✓ Neon JS SDK is ready! Here's what you can do:\n- Visit /auth/sign-up to create an account\n- Visit /auth/sign-in to log in\n- The UserButton shows a dropdown when signed in\n- Visit /account/settings to manage your profile\n- Query your database with `client.from('table').select()`\n- Google and GitHub OAuth are enabled by default\"\n\n---\n\n## Reference Resources\n\n**Setup Guides:**\n- [Complete Setup Guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules/main/neon-plugin/skills/neon-js/guides/setup.md) - Step-by-step walkthrough\n- [Auth Setup Reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules/main/references/neon-auth-setup.md) - Framework-specific auth patterns\n- [Data API Reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules/main/references/neon-js-data-api.md) - PostgREST query patterns\n\n**UI & Components:**\n- [UI Components Reference](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules/main/references/neon-auth-ui.md) - All UI components and provider config\n\n**Troubleshooting:**\n- [Common Mistakes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules/main/references/neon-auth-common-mistakes.md) - Import paths, adapter patterns, CSS\n- [Troubleshooting Guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules/main/references/neon-auth-troubleshooting.md) - Error solutions\n\n**Code Generation:**\n- [Code Generation Rules](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules/main/references/code-generation-rules.md) - Import and CSS strategies\n\n**Main Documentation:**\n- [neon-js.mdc](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules/main/neon-js.mdc) - Quick reference and patterns\n- [neon-auth.mdc](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules/main/neon-auth.mdc) - Auth-specific patterns\n\n---\n\n## Success Criteria\n\nSetup is complete when:\n- [ ] Package installed (@neondatabase/neon-js)\n- [ ] Environment variables configured (auth URL + data API URL)\n- [ ] Auth client created and exported\n- [ ] Database client created and exported\n- [ ] (If Next.js) API route handler created\n- [ ] (Optional) TypeScript types generated\n- [ ] (If using UI) Provider configured\n- [ ] User can authenticate successfully\n- [ ] Database queries return data\n- [ ] No console errors\n\n---\n\n**Template Version**: 1.1.0  \n**Last Updated**: 2025-12-09  \n**Source Repository**: https://github.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules\n",

      "rawContent": "# MCP Prompt Templates\n\nLightweight prompt templates for the Neon MCP server that link to comprehensive guides in this repository.\n\n## Purpose\n\nThese templates provide structure and navigation for MCP prompts while keeping the actual content in the ai-rules repository. This ensures:\n- **Single source of truth** for all documentation\n- **Easy maintenance** - update docs in one place\n- **Automatic updates** - MCP prompts use latest version from main branch via GitHub raw URLs\n- **No duplication** - content lives in guides, references, and .mdc files\n\n## Template Architecture\n\nEach template follows the **progressive disclosure** pattern from Claude Code skills best practices:\n\n1. **Communication Style** - How the AI should interact with users\n2. **Context Detection** - Auto-detect framework, package manager, existing setup\n3. **Package Selection** - Guide user to right package for their needs\n4. **Framework Routing** - Link to appropriate detailed guide based on context\n5. **Key Configuration** - Highlight critical paths and common mistakes\n6. **Validation Steps** - Guide user through testing\n7. **Troubleshooting Links** - Load error resources only when needed\n8. **Comprehensive Reference** - Link to full .mdc file for deep dives\n\n## Available Templates\n\n### neon-auth-setup.md\n**Purpose**: Interactive authentication setup guide\n\n**Covers**:\n- Package selection (auth-only vs full SDK)\n- Framework detection (Next.js, React SPA, Node.js)\n- Links to detailed Next.js guide\n- React SPA and Node.js adaptations\n- Critical import paths and CSS strategy\n- Validation and troubleshooting\n\n**Links to**:\n- `/references/neon-auth-setup.md` (canonical setup reference for all frameworks)\n- `/neon-plugin/skills/neon-auth/guides/nextjs-setup.md` (Next.js detailed guide)\n- `/neon-plugin/skills/neon-auth/guides/react-spa-setup.md` (React SPA detailed guide)\n- `/neon-auth.mdc` (comprehensive reference)\n- `/references/neon-auth-common-mistakes.md`\n- `/references/neon-auth-troubleshooting.md`\n\n### neon-js-setup.md\n**Purpose**: Interactive full SDK setup (auth + database queries)\n\n**Covers**:\n- Package confirmation (full SDK vs auth-only)\n- Framework detection\n- Links to detailed setup guide\n- React SPA and Node.js adaptations\n- Database query patterns (PostgREST syntax)\n- Type generation workflow\n- Validation for both auth and database\n\n**Links to**:\n- `/neon-plugin/skills/neon-js/guides/setup.md` (complete setup guide)\n- `/references/neon-auth-setup.md` (auth setup reference)\n- `/references/neon-js-data-api.md` (database query patterns)\n- `/neon-js.mdc` (comprehensive reference)\n- `/references/neon-auth-common-mistakes.md`\n- `/references/neon-js-imports.md`\n\n## Template Structure\n\nAll templates follow this structure:\n\n```markdown\n# [Package] Setup (MCP Prompt Template)\n\n> Purpose statement\n\n## Communication Style\n[Interaction guidelines for AI]\n\n## Step 1: Detect Project Context\n[Auto-detection commands]\n\n## Step 2: Package/Framework Selection\n[Decision logic and routing]\n\n## Step 3: Load Framework-Specific Guide\n[Links to detailed guides]\n\n## Step 4-N: Key Configuration Points\n[Critical paths, common mistakes]\n\n## Troubleshooting Resources\n[Links to error guides]\n\n## Comprehensive Reference\n[Link to main .mdc file]\n\n## Success Criteria\n[Checklist for completion]\n```\n\n## GitHub Raw URL Format\n\nAll links use this format:\n```\nhttps://raw.githubusercontent.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules/main/[path-to-file]\n```\n\nThis ensures:\n- ✅ Always loads latest version from main branch\n- ✅ Fast delivery via GitHub's CDN\n- ✅ Works from any AI assistant\n- ✅ No authentication required for public repos\n\n## Benefits of This Approach\n\n### For Users\n- Consistent experience across Claude Code, MCP, and other tools\n- Always get latest documentation\n- Clear, step-by-step guidance\n\n### For Maintainers\n- Update docs in ONE place (ai-rules repo)\n- MCP prompts automatically use new version\n- Easy to test (just update guide and test MCP prompt)\n- Version control for all content\n\n### For AI Assistants\n- Progressive disclosure (load details only when needed)\n- Clear navigation structure\n- Comprehensive reference available when needed\n- Troubleshooting resources on-demand\n\n## Versioning\n\nTemplates include version information in footer:\n```markdown\n---\n**Template Version**: 1.0.0\n**Last Updated**: 2025-12-09\n**Source Repository**: https://github.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules\n```\n\nUpdate version when making breaking changes to template structure.\n\n## Contributing\n\nWhen creating or updating templates:\n\n1. **Keep them lightweight** - Focus on navigation and linking, not duplicating content\n2. **Link, don't duplicate** - Reference existing guides\n3. **Follow structure** - Use standard sections\n4. **Test thoroughly** - Verify all links work\n5. **Update version** - Increment on breaking changes\n\n## Related Documentation\n\n- [Implementation Plan](../plans/mcp-prompts-github-integration.md)\n- [Claude Code Skills Best Practices](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills)\n- [Neon Auth Guide](../neon-auth.mdc)\n- [Neon JS Guide](../neon-js.mdc)\n",

      "contentPreview": "Complete integration plugin for using Neon Postgres databases with Claude Code, featuring guided skills and MCP server integration.\n**Guided Skills**: Step-by-step workflows for common Neon tasks\n**MCP Integration**: Real-time Neon resource management through Model Context Protocol\n**Knowledge Insta",
      "rawContent": "# Neon Claude Code Plugin\n\nComplete integration plugin for using Neon Postgres databases with Claude Code, featuring guided skills and MCP server integration.\n\n## Features\n\n- **Guided Skills**: Step-by-step workflows for common Neon tasks\n- **MCP Integration**: Real-time Neon resource management through Model Context Protocol\n- **Knowledge Installation**: Add Neon best practices to your project's AI knowledge base\n\n## Available Skills\n\n### neon-drizzle\nSet up and integrate Drizzle ORM with Neon Postgres databases. Includes comprehensive guides for:\n- New project setup\n- Existing project integration\n- Schema-only workflows\n- Migration troubleshooting\n\n### neon-serverless\nConnect to Neon databases in serverless environments with the Neon Serverless driver. Optimize for:\n- Edge functions\n- Vercel deployments\n- AWS Lambda\n- Low latency and connection pooling\n\n### neon-toolkit\nCreate and manage ephemeral Neon databases for testing and prototyping. Perfect for:\n- CI/CD pipelines\n- Test isolation\n- Quick development workflows\n\n## Knowledge Installation\n\nAfter completing a skill workflow, you can optionally install Neon best practices to your project's AI knowledge base.\n\n### How It Works\n\n1. Complete any Neon skill workflow (Drizzle, Serverless, Toolkit, etc.)\n2. I'll detect your project's AI structure:\n   - **Cursor IDE**: `.cursor/rules/`\n   - **Claude Code**: `CLAUDE.md` or `.claude/`\n   - **Custom**: `agents.md`, `.ai/`, or other locations\n3. I'll ask if you want to install documentation\n4. I'll copy the relevant `.mdc` files with source attribution\n5. Your AI assistant can now reference these patterns automatically\n\n### What Gets Installed\n\nEach skill installs its relevant best practices:\n\n- **neon-drizzle**: Drizzle ORM integration, connection adapters, schema patterns\n- **neon-serverless**: Serverless connections, pooling, edge runtime considerations\n- **neon-toolkit**: Ephemeral database creation, testing workflows\n\n### No AI Structure Yet?\n\nIf your project doesn't have an AI knowledge structure yet:\n- I can create a `CLAUDE.md` file for you\n- Or you can run `/init` in Claude Code first\n- Or set up Cursor rules manually\n\n### For Developers\n\nSkills use a workflow-based approach. See `shared/workflows/install-knowledge.md` for the universal workflow that guides me through the installation process.\n\n## Getting Started\n\n1. Install the plugin in Claude Code\n2. Activate a skill based on your needs\n3. Follow the guided workflow\n4. Optionally install knowledge to your project\n\n## MCP Server Integration\n\nThis plugin connects to Neon's remote MCP server for real-time resource management. The MCP server provides:\n- Project listing and creation\n- Branch management\n- Database operations\n- Connection string generation\n\nConfiguration is handled automatically through `.mcp.json`.\n\n## Repository Structure\n\n```\nneon-plugin/\n├── .claude-plugin/\n│   └── plugin.json        # Plugin metadata\n├── .mcp.json              # MCP server configuration\n└── skills/\n    ├── add-neon-docs/\n    │   ├── SKILL.md\n    │   ├── install-knowledge.md        # Workflow for knowledge installation\n    │   └── skill-knowledge-map.json    # Metadata for knowledge installation\n    ├── neon-drizzle/\n    │   ├── SKILL.md\n    │   ├── guides/        # Step-by-step workflow guides\n    │   ├── references/    # Technical reference docs\n    │   ├── scripts/       # Utility scripts\n    │   └── templates/     # Code templates\n    ├── neon-serverless/\n    │   └── SKILL.md\n    └── neon-toolkit/\n        └── SKILL.md\n```\n\n## Contributing\n\nTo add a new skill or update existing ones:\n1. Follow the skill structure pattern\n2. Update `skills/add-neon-docs/skill-knowledge-map.json` if adding knowledge files\n3. Reference the `add-neon-docs` skill at the end of your SKILL.md\n4. Test the workflow thoroughly\n\n## Resources\n\n- [Neon Documentation](https://neon.com/docs/)\n- [Claude Code Documentation](https://docs.claude.com/en/docs/claude-code/quickstart)\n- [MCP Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io)\n\n## License\n\nSee the main repository for license information.\n",

      "contentPreview": "**When to use**: When the user wants to add Neon's best practices reference links to their project's AI documentation.\n**Required parameter**:  (e.g., \"neon-drizzle\", \"neon-serverless\", \"neon-toolkit\")\n---\n> **IMPORTANT - Working Directory Context**\n>\n> This skill reads metadata from its own skill d",
      "rawContent": "# Install Neon Knowledge to Project - Agent Workflow\n\n**When to use**: When the user wants to add Neon's best practices reference links to their project's AI documentation.\n\n**Required parameter**: `SKILL_NAME` (e.g., \"neon-drizzle\", \"neon-serverless\", \"neon-toolkit\")\n\n---\n\n> **IMPORTANT - Working Directory Context**\n>\n> This skill reads metadata from its own skill directory (`skill-knowledge-map.json`), but **ALL project file operations** (reading/writing `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, etc.) **MUST happen in the current working directory**.\n>\n> - ✅ Read skill metadata from skill directory (absolute paths provided by system)\n> - ✅ Read/write project files using **relative paths only** (e.g., `CLAUDE.md`, `.cursor/rules.md`)\n> - ❌ Never construct project file paths using absolute paths or the skill's base directory\n\n---\n\n## Step 1: Load Skill Metadata\n\nRead the skill metadata file to get the reference URLs.\n\nThe metadata file is bundled with this skill at:\n```\nskill-knowledge-map.json\n```\n\nUse the Read tool to read the local file, then parse the JSON content.\n\nExtract the metadata for the current `SKILL_NAME` from the JSON.\n\nStore this information - you'll need:\n- `displayName`: Human-readable skill name\n- `files`: Array of .mdc files (each with `url`, `filename`, `description`)\n\nIf the skill is not found in metadata, inform the user and exit.\n\n---\n\n## Step 2: Detect AI Documentation File\n\nUse your existing tools to detect where to add the reference links in the **current working directory**. **This is a read-only check - no files are created yet.**\n\nCheck in this priority order:\n\n### 2.1 Check for CLAUDE.md (most common)\n\nUse the Glob tool to search for `CLAUDE.md` in the current working directory:\n```\npattern: \"CLAUDE.md\"\n```\n\n**If found**: Target is `CLAUDE.md` file\n\n### 2.2 Check for AGENTS.md (custom AI docs)\n\nUse the Glob tool to search for `AGENTS.md`:\n```\npattern: \"AGENTS.md\"\n```\n\n**If found**: Target is `AGENTS.md` file\n\n### 2.3 Check for Cursor rules file\n\nUse the Glob tool to search for Cursor       "contentPreview": "> **Complete Walkthrough**: This is a self-contained, step-by-step guide with its own numbered phases (Phase 1-8).\n> Follow each phase in order for a full Neon Auth setup in Next.js App Router.\nComplete guide for setting up Neon Auth with Next.js App Router.\nRemember to run the neon-plugin:add-neon-",
      "rawContent": "# Next.js Auth Setup\n\n> **Complete Walkthrough**: This is a self-contained, step-by-step guide with its own numbered phases (Phase 1-8).\n> Follow each phase in order for a full Neon Auth setup in Next.js App Router.\n\nComplete guide for setting up Neon Auth with Next.js App Router.\n\n### Important:\n- Remember to run the neon-plugin:add-neon-docs skill with the parameter SKILL_NAME=\"neon-auth\" after completing the guide.\n\n## Table of Contents\n\n- [Next.js Auth Setup](#nextjs-auth-setup)\n    - [Important:](#important)\n  - [Table of Contents](#table-of-contents)\n  - [Workflow Checklist](#workflow-checklist)\n  - [Phase 1: Context Detection](#phase-1-context-detection)\n  - [Phase 2: Installation](#phase-2-installation)\n  - [Phase 3: Environment Configuration](#phase-3-environment-configuration)\n  - [Phase 4: API Route Setup](#phase-4-api-route-setup)\n  - [Phase 5: Auth Client Configuration](#phase-5-auth-client-configuration)\n  - [Phase 6: UI Provider Setup (Optional)](#phase-6-ui-provider-setup-optional)\n    - [6.1. Import CSS](#61-import-css)\n    - [6.2. Create Auth Provider](#62-create-auth-provider)\n    - [6.3. Wrap App in Provider](#63-wrap-app-in-provider)\n    - [6.4. Add Navbar with Session Info](#64-add-navbar-with-session-info)\n  - [Phase 7: Auth Pages Setup (Optional)](#phase-7-auth-pages-setup-optional)\n  - [Phase 8: Validation \\& Testing](#phase-8-validation--testing)\n    - [8.1. Manual Testing Checklist](#81-manual-testing-checklist)\n  - [Phase 9: Add Best Practices References](#phase-9-add-best-practices-references)\n  - [Setup Complete!](#setup-complete)\n\n---\n\n## Workflow Checklist\n\nWhen following this guide, I will track these high-level tasks:\n\n- [ ] Detect project context (package manager, Next.js version, existing auth)\n- [ ] Install @neondatabase/auth package\n- [ ] Configure environment variables (auth URL)\n- [ ] Create API route handler at /api/auth/[...path]\n- [ ] Set up auth client for client components\n- [ ] (Optional) Set up UI provider with pre-built components\n- [ ] (Optional) Create auth pages (/auth/sign-in, etc.)\n- [ ] Validate setup and test authentication flow\n- [ ] Add Neon Auth best practices to project docs\n\n---\n\n## Phase 1: Context Detection\n\nAuto-detect project context:\n\n**Check Package Manager:**\n```bash\nls package-lock.json  # -> npm\nls bun.lockb          # -> bun\nls pnpm-lock.yaml     # -> pnpm\nls yarn.lock          # -> yarn\n```\n\n**Check Next.js Version:**\n```bash\ngrep '\"next\"' package.json\n```\nEnsure Next.js 13+ with App Router (pages in `app/` directory).\n\n**Check Existing Setup:**\n```bash\nls app/api/auth        # Auth routes exist?\nls lib/auth            # Auth client exists?\ngrep '@neondatabase' package.json  # Already installed?\n```\n\n**Check for Tailwind:**\n```bash\nls tailwind.config.js tailwind.config.ts 2>/dev/null\n```\n\n**Check Environment Files:**\n```bash\nls .env .env.local\n```\n\n## Phase 2: Installation\n\nBased on detection, install the auth package:\n\n```bash\n[package-manager] add @neondatabase/auth\n```\n\nReplace `[package-manager]` with your detected package manager (npm install, pnpm add, yarn add, bun add).\n\n## Phase 3: Environment Configuration\n\n**Outcome**: A working `.env.local` file with the Neon Auth URL.\n\nCreate or update `.env.local`:\n\n```bash\n# Neon Auth URL - get this from your Neon dashboard\n# Format: https://ep-xxx.neonauth.c-2.us-east-2.aws.neon.build/dbname/auth\nNEON_AUTH_BASE_URL=your-neon-auth-url\nNEXT_PUBLIC_NEON_AUTH_URL=your-neon-auth-url\n```\n\n**Where to find your Auth URL:**\n1. Go to your Neon project dashboard\n2. Navigate to the \"Auth\" tab\n3. Copy the Auth URL\n\n**Important:** Both variables are needed:\n- `NEON_AUTH_BASE_URL` - Used by server-side API routes\n- `NEXT_PUBLIC_NEON_AUTH_URL` - Used by client-side components (prefixed with NEXT_PUBLIC_)\n\nAdd to `.gitignore` if not already present:\n```\n.env.local\n```\n\n## Phase 4: API Route Setup\n\nCreate the API route handler for authentication endpoints:\n\n**Create file:** `app/api/auth/[...path]/route.ts`\n\n```typescript\nimport { authApiHandler } from \"@neondatabase/auth/next\";\n\nexport const { GET, POST } = authApiHandler();\n```\n\nThis creates endpoints for:\n- `/api/auth/sign-in` - Sign in\n- `/api/auth/sign-up` - Sign up\n- `/api/auth/sign-out` - Sign out\n- `/api/auth/session` - Get session\n- And other auth-related endpoints\n\n## Phase 5: Auth Client Configuration\n\nCreate the auth client for use in client components:\n\n**Create file:** `lib/auth/client.ts`\n\n```typescript\nimport { createAuthClient } from \"@neondatabase/auth/next\";\n\nexport const authClient = createAuthClient();\n```\n\n**Usage in components:**\n\n```typescript\n\"use client\";\n\nimport { authClient } from \"@/lib/auth/client\";\n\nfunction AuthStatus() {\n  const session = authClient.useSession();\n\n  if (session.isPending) return <div>Loading...<\/div>;\n  if (!session.data) return <SignInButton />;\n\n  return (\n    <div>\n      <p>Hello, {session.data.user.name}<\/p>\n      <button onClick={() => authClient.signOut()}>Sign Out<\/button>\n    <\/div>\n  );\n}\n\nfunction SignInButton() {\n  return (\n    <button onClick={() => authClient.signIn.email({\n      email: \"user@example.com\",\n      password: \"password\"\n    })}>\n      Sign In\n    <\/button>\n  );\n}\n```\n\n## Phase 6: UI Provider Setup (Optional)\n\nSkip this phase if you're building custom auth forms. Use this if you want pre-built UI components.\n\n### 6.1. Import CSS\n\nAuth UI **automatically inherits your app's existing theme**. If you have CSS variables like `--primary`, `--background`, etc. defined (from Tailwind, shadcn/ui, or custom CSS), auth components use them with no configuration.\n\nImport order doesn't matter - auth styles are in `@layer neon-auth`, so your styles always win.\n\n**If using Tailwind (tailwind.config.{js,ts} exists):**\n\nAdd to your global CSS file (e.g., `app/globals.css`):\n```css\n@import '@neondatabase/auth/ui/tailwind';\n```\n\n**If NOT using Tailwind:**\n\nAdd to `app/layout.tsx`:\n```typescript\nimport \"@neondatabase/auth/ui/css\";\n```\n\n**Warning:** Never import both - causes 94KB of duplicate styles.\n\n**Auth-specific customization:** To customize auth components differently from your main app, use `--neon-*` prefix variables. See the [theming guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules/main/references/neon-js-theming.md) for details.\n\n### 6.2. Create Auth Provider\n\n**Create file:** `app/auth-provider.tsx`\n\n```typescript\n\"use client\";\n\nimport { NeonAuthUIProvider } from \"@neondatabase/auth/react/ui\";\nimport { authClient } from \"@/lib/auth/client\";\nimport { useRouter } from \"next/navigation\";\nimport Link from \"next/link\";\n\nexport function AuthProvider({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {\n  const router = useRouter();\n  return (\n    <NeonAuthUIProvider\n      authClient={authClient}\n      navigate={router.push}\n      replace={router.replace}\n      onSessionChange={() => router.refresh()}\n      Link={Link}\n    >\n      {children}\n    <\/NeonAuthUIProvider>\n  );\n}\n```\n\n**To add social login buttons**, add the `social` prop:\n```typescript\n<NeonAuthUIProvider\n  authClient={authClient}\n  navigate={router.push}\n  replace={router.replace}\n  onSessionChange={() => router.refresh()}\n  Link={Link}\n  social={{\n    // TWO configs required: 1) Enable providers in Neon Console, 2) List them here\n    providers: [\"google\", \"github\"]\n  }}\n>\n  {children}\n<\/NeonAuthUIProvider>\n```\n\n### 6.3. Wrap App in Provider\n\n**Update:** `app/layout.tsx`\n\n```typescript\nimport { AuthProvider } from \"./auth-provider\";\n\nexport default function RootLayout({\n  children,\n}: {\n  children: React.ReactNode;\n}) {\n  return (\n    <html lang=\"en\">\n      <body>\n        <AuthProvider>{children}<\/AuthProvider>\n      <\/body>\n    <\/html>\n  );\n}\n```\n\n### 6.4. Add Navbar with Session Info\n\nCreate a navbar component that shows the user's session status:\n\n**Create file:** `components/navbar.tsx`\n\n```typescript\n\"use client\";\n\nimport { UserButton, SignedIn, SignedOut } from \"@neondatabase/auth/react/ui\";\nimport Link from \"next/link\";\n\nexport function Navbar() {\n  return (\n    <nav className=\"flex items-center justify-between p-4 border-b\">\n      <Link href=\"/\">My App<\/Link>\n      <div className=\"flex items-center gap-4\">\n        <SignedOut>\n          <Link href=\"/auth/sign-in\">Sign In<\/Link>\n        <\/SignedOut>\n        <SignedIn>\n          <UserButton />\n        <\/SignedIn>\n      <\/div>\n    <\/nav>\n  );\n}\n```\n\n**Add to layout:** Update `app/layout.tsx` to include the navbar:\n\n```typescript\nimport { AuthProvider } from \"./auth-provider\";\nimport { Navbar } from \"@/components/navbar\";\n\nexport default function RootLayout({\n  children,\n}: {\n  children: React.ReactNode;\n}) {\n  return (\n    <html lang=\"en\">\n      <body>\n        <AuthProvider>\n          <Navbar />\n          {children}\n        <\/AuthProvider>\n      <\/body>\n    <\/html>\n  );\n}\n```\n\n**Components explained:**\n- `<SignedOut>` - Only renders children when user is NOT authenticated\n- `<SignedIn>` - Only renders children when user IS authenticated\n- `<UserButton />` - Displays user avatar with dropdown menu (sign out, account settings)\n\n## Phase 7: Auth Pages Setup (Optional)\n\nSkip this phase if you're using custom auth forms. Use this for pre-built auth pages.\n\n**Create file:** `app/auth/[path]/page.tsx`\n\n```typescript\nimport { AuthView } from \"@neondatabase/auth/react/ui\";\nimport { authViewPaths } from \"@neondatabase/auth/react/ui/server\";\n\nexport const dynamicParams = false;\n\nexport function generateStaticParams() {\n  return Object.values(authViewPaths).map((path) => ({ path }));\n}\n\nexport default async function AuthPage({\n  params,\n}: {\n  params: Promise<{ path: string }>;\n}) {\n  const { path } = await params;\n  return <AuthView pathname={path} />;\n}\n```\n\nThis creates routes for:\n- `/auth/sign-in` - Sign in page\n- `/auth/sign-up` - Sign up page\n- `/auth/forgot-password` - Password reset request\n- `/auth/reset-password` - Password reset form\n- `/auth/magic-link` - Magic link sign in\n- `/auth/two-factor` - Two-factor authentication\n- `/auth/callback` - OAuth callback\n- `/auth/sign-out` - Sign out page\n\n## Phase 8: Validation & Testing\n\n### 8.1. Manual Testing Checklist\n\n- [ ] Start development server: `npm run dev`\n- [ ] Navigate to `/auth/sign-up` (if using pre-built pages)\n- [ ] Create a test account\n- [ ] Sign out\n- [ ] Sign back in\n- [ ] Verify session persists across page refresh\n- [ ] Check browser console for errors\n\n**Common Issues:**\n- \"Module not found\" - Check import paths match subpath exports\n- Session not persisting - Verify API route is correctly configured\n- CSS not loading - Check you imported CSS in layout (only one method)\n\nFor detailed error resolution, see:\n- [Troubleshooting Guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules/main/references/neon-auth-troubleshooting.md)\n- [Common Mistakes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/neondatabase-labs/ai-rules/main/references/neon-auth-common-mistakes.md)\n\n## Phase 9: Add Best Practices References\n\nBefore executing the add-neon-docs skill, provide a summary of everything that has been done:\n\n\"Neon Auth integration is complete! Now adding documentation references...\"\n\nThen execute the neon-plugin:add-neon-docs skill with the parameter SKILL_NAME=\"neon-auth\"\n\nThis will add reference links to Neon Auth best practices documentation in your project's AI documentation file.\n\n---\n\n## Setup Complete!\n\nYour Neon Auth integration is ready to use.\n\n**What's working:**\n- Authentication API routes at `/api/auth/*`\n- Client-side auth hooks via `authClient.useSession()`\n- (If configured) Pre-built UI components and auth pages\n\n**Next steps:**\n- Add protected routes using session checks\n- Customize UI theme (see neon-auth.mdc for theming)\n- Set up social OAuth providers in Neon dashboard\n",
      "renderedContent": "<h1>Next.js Auth Setup<\/h1>\n<blockquote>\n<p><strong>Complete Walkthrough<\/strong>: This is a self-contained, step-by-step guide with its own numbered phases (Phase 1-8).\nFollow each phase in order for a full Neon Auth setup in Next.js App Router.<\/p>\n<\/blockquote>\n<p>Complete guide for setting up Neon Auth with Next.js App Router.<\/p>\n<h3>Important:<\/h3>\n<ul>\n<li>Remember to run the neon-plugin:add-neon-docs skill with the parameter SKILL_NAME=&quot;neon-auth&quot; after completing the guide.<\/li>\n<\/ul>\n<h2>Table of Contents<\/h2>\n<ul>\n<li><a href=\"#nextjs-auth-setup\">Next.js Auth Setup<\/a><ul>\n<li><a href=\"#important\">Important:<\/a><\/li>\n<li><a href=\"#table-of-contents\">Table of Contents<\/a><\/li>\n<li><a href=\"#workflow-checklist\">Workflow Checklist<\/a><\/li>\n<li><a href=\"#phase-1-context-detection\">Phase 1: Context Detection<\/a><\/li>\n<li><a href=\"#phase-2-installation\">Phase 2: Installation<\/a><\/li>\n<li><a href=\"#phase-3-environment-configuration\">Phase 3: Environment Configuration<\/a><\/li>\n<li><a href=\"#phase-4-api-route-setup\">Phase 4: API Route Setup<\/a><\/li>\n<li><a href=\"#phase-5-auth-client-configuration\">Phase 5: Auth Client Configuration<\/a><\/li>\n<li><a href=\"#phase-6-ui-provider-setup-optional\">Phase 6: UI Provider Setup (Optional)<\/a><ul>\n<li><a href=\"#61-import-css\">6.1.
